guest.titre: Personal Finance Expert, Author, and Host of The Table
guest.bio_context: Anthony O'Neal became homeless at age 19 and accumulated $35,000 in debt, with approximately $32,000 of it going to collections. He rebuilt his life by following Dave Ramsey's seven baby steps and later worked at Ramsey Solutions for approximately six years as the youth financial literacy speaker. He became a number one national bestselling author and built one of the largest African-American youth ministries in the world, with 3,000 to 4,000 people at youth conferences, where he taught financial literacy in high schools.

pending_qa.q: What is Anthony O'Neal's philosophy on credit cards and how does he use them today?
pending_qa.r: Anthony O'Neal believes roughly 90% of everyday people are not responsible enough to have a credit card, and recommends being out of debt for a minimum of 24 months before touching one. He personally keeps only one card — an Amex charge card — which he pays off every single Monday, and he refuses to use any card that allows carrying a balance, because he views paying interest as a penalty.

pending_qa.q: How does Anthony O'Neal define financial freedom and what does it look like in his daily life?
pending_qa.r: Anthony O'Neal defines freedom as being able to make decisions based on his own habits rather than being enslaved to debt. Concretely, this means taking every Friday off to play golf and go to dinner, taking a two-week cash-paid cruise to Greece, and giving his entire company team the full month of July off with full pay — all made possible by running a business with zero consumer debt.

pending_qa.q: What steps did Anthony O'Neal take to get out of debt and turn his story into a career?
pending_qa.r: Anthony O'Neal educated himself by reading Rich Dad Poor Dad by Robert Kiyosaki and Total Money Makeover by Dave Ramsey, then committed to following Dave Ramsey's seven baby steps. He began teaching financial literacy as a youth pastor, going into high schools to teach students about scholarships, credit cards, and credit reports, which eventually caught the attention of Ramsey Solutions and launched his professional career.

pending_qa.q: What does Anthony O'Neal say about the gap between how people appear financially and their actual financial situation?
pending_qa.r: Anthony O'Neal states that 76% of luxury buyers are faking their wealth and that 71% of Americans are living paycheck to paycheck. Of that 71%, he says 90% report that missing a single paycheck would cause serious financial crisis in their lives.

pending_qa.q: What is Anthony O'Neal's stance on Dave Ramsey's teachings and where does he diverge?
pending_qa.r: Anthony O'Neal deeply respects Dave Ramsey, credits the seven baby steps with making him consumer debt-free, and worked at Ramsey Solutions for approximately six years. However, since leaving, he has evolved his philosophy — most notably on credit cards — believing that people who are out of debt for at least 24 months and have built healthy financial habits can responsibly use a credit card like an Amex charge card.
